items.item_text: resume

Must possess a valid California Driver's License to drive a County or University vehicle. Ability and means to travel on a flexible schedule as needed; proof of liability damage insurance on vehicle used is required. Reimbursement of job-related travel will be reimbursed according to University policies.
High school diploma or equivalent experience.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

Provide administrative office support for the county director and advisors. Serve as first point of contact for the office; manage walk-ins, answer and route phone calls to appropriate parties, provide general program and procedural information.
Problem-solve clientele issues before forwarding to appropriate staff/advisors.

Compose, prepare, edit newsletters, forms, reports, tables, spreadsheets, memos, and general correspondence and other documents using word processing and graphics software from draft through final versions. Assist advisors in compiling and preparing grant proposals.

Provide administrative support and intercede with Business Operations Center (BOC) to troubleshoot travel report issues for staff/advisers and serve as a delegate in processing travel and entertainment reimbursements and corporate card payments for the county director.

Coordinate location and meeting logistics for events. Troubleshoot basic tech issues and resolve for staff when possible. Serve as contact person for routine building maintenance and request county and/or UC IT support for more complex technology or telecommunications issues. Prepare outgoing and process incoming mail. Order, inventory and maintain office supplies.

Provide guidance to advisors and staff on procedures, practices, and implementing policies. Anticipate and prepare reports to support county director, advisors, and staff queries. Maintain updated organizational chart, staff office and emergency contact list. Perform role of ANR Safety Coordinator, enforce safe practices in office, and may attend quarterly Safety Team meetings.

Track account milestones and end dates, analyze/recommend budget line-item adjustments for advisors' accounts and program development expenses; initiate/prepare fiscal projections and make recommendations to county director. Prepare annual county expenditure, budget and variance reports for UCOP/ANR Resource Planning & Management office. Consolidate annual program work plans/budgets for reporting.

Work with ANR Human Resources Unit (HR) and supervisor to coordinate new hire, personnel, and separation actions. Assist new employees with completion of UC employment forms provided by HR, and obtain UC ANR logins, email, access to server, office procedures etc. Maintain confidential personnel, safety training, and worker compensation/accident files. Track personnel contract ending dates, coordinate with advisors/staff to notify the BOC of funding changes and extensions of appointments, and review accuracy of payroll distribution percentages by funding account. Manage sensitive and confidential information regarding bargaining unit issues. File and track Worker's Compensation claims and staff leave requests. Liaison with staff/academics regarding the submission of online timesheets. Collect and receive all absence slips and changes to work schedules. Maintain a master calendar of approved staff vacation/sick leave for county directors and advisors to match online timesheet reporting. Review ergonomic needs of staff and manage interface with ANR Risk & Safety Services

Maintain UCCE Alameda website using Site Builder software. Modify county director’s program page as requested, create web pages and surveys for events and activities. Maintain contact database for advisors. Oversee administrative access approval to Master Gardener/4-H/Master Composter/Master Food Preserver volunteers and liaison/trouble-shoot with UC tech support.
Ability to maintain strict confidentiality of information.
Experience with bookkeeping, accounting, and invoice processing, including independently gathering, organizing, and analyzing financial information.
Experience establishing goals and priorities, organizing and coordinating multiple and complex projects simultaneously and with competing deadlines.
Strong attention to detail, with a demonstrated commitment to accuracy and thoroughness.
Thorough computer skills and experience using Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, Adobe, and multiple internet browsers.
Thorough knowledge in administrative procedures and processes, including drafting correspondence and maintaining files and databases.
Skills to maintain calendars for multiple individuals using computer technology.
Ability to handle scheduling and logistical arrangements for travel and meetings.
Requires good verbal and written communication skills, active listening, critical thinking, multitasking, and time management skills.
Knowledge and/or experience with web page design and content.
Experience working in a complex, multi-location public university or higher education system, or in a medium-to-large nonprofit or foundation.
Maintains interpersonal and work leadership skills to provide guidance to other nonexempt personnel.
Special Conditions of Employment:
Must comply with regulatory agency reporting requirements (California's Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act).

As of January 1, 2014, ANR is a smoke- and tobacco-free environment in which smoking, the use of smokeless tobacco products, and the use of unregulated nicotine products (e-cigarettes), are strictly prohibited.
